questions.stem: Panchayati Raj (local self-government in rural areas) was given constitutional status by which amendment?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment (1992) inserted Part IX (Articles 243-243O) and the Eleventh Schedule (29 subjects) into the Constitution, giving three-tier Panchayati Raj a constitutional basis. The 74th Amendment (same year) did the parallel job for urban local bodies (Part IXA, Articles 243P-243ZG, Twelfth Schedule, 18 subjects). The 42nd Amendment (1976) is unrelated — it added Fundamental Duties.

questions.stem: Under the 73rd Amendment, the minimum reservation of seats for women in Panchayats is:
questions.explanation: Art 243D — minimum 1/3 seats reserved for women in Panchayats at all three tiers (plus proportional reservations for SC / ST). Many states (Bihar 2006, Andhra, Karnataka, etc.) have voluntarily raised it to 50 %. The 2023 Women's Reservation Act (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam) extends 33 % reservation to Lok Sabha and state Assemblies, but will take effect after the next delimitation.

questions.stem: The three-tier Panchayati Raj structure consists of Gram Panchayat (village), Panchayat Samiti (block) and:
questions.explanation: 73rd Amendment mandates a three-tier system in states with population > 20 lakh — Gram Panchayat (village level), Panchayat Samiti (intermediate block level), Zila Parishad (district level). Smaller states may have two tiers. Municipal Corporations / Councils / Nagar Panchayats are urban bodies under the 74th Amendment. Cantonment Boards operate under the Cantonments Act (military / defence areas).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) was the first to recommend a three-tier Panchayati Raj structure in India. The first state to implement its recommendations (1959) was:
questions.explanation: Rajasthan was the first state to implement the Balwant Rai Mehta recommendations on 2 October 1959, with Prime Minister Nehru inaugurating the first Panchayati Raj body in Nagaur district. Andhra Pradesh followed almost immediately the same year. The Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) later recommended a two-tier system. Panchayati Raj reached constitutional status only with the 73rd Amendment, 1992.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The term of a Panchayat — fixed by the Constitution — is:
questions.explanation: Art 243E — every Panchayat has a fixed term of five years unless dissolved earlier. If dissolved earlier, fresh elections must be held within 6 months. The original term ends automatically at five years; a state cannot, by ordinary legislation, extend it. A similar 5-year rule applies to urban local bodies under the 74th Amendment.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Panchayat elections are conducted by the:

options.option_text: State government through the District Collector

questions.explanation: Art 243K — each state has its own State Election Commission (SEC) that is constitutionally separate from the Central Election Commission. The SEC superintends, directs and controls preparation of electoral rolls and conduct of elections to Panchayats (and under Art 243ZA, municipalities). The ECI handles only Parliament, state Assemblies, President and VP elections.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 'Gram Sabha' mentioned in the 73rd Amendment is a body consisting of:

options.option_text: All elected members of a Panchayat
All adult registered voters of the village

questions.explanation: Gram Sabha (Art 243A) — the village-level general body of all persons whose names are on the electoral rolls of the village. It is a direct democratic institution — it meets to approve the Panchayat's development plans, discuss annual accounts, beneficiary lists under government schemes, etc. The Gram Panchayat is the elected executive body. PESA (1996) gives Gram Sabhas in Fifth Schedule (tribal) areas wider powers over land and forest resources.
